units.zh: 文惠皇太后王氏，開平初追諡。
units.en: Empress Dowager Wenhui (Wang) received her posthumous title early in the Kaiping era.
units.literal: Empress Dowager Wenhui, née Wang, was given a posthumous title at the beginning of Kaiping.

units.zh: 太祖性孝願，奉太后未嘗小失色，朝夕視膳，為士君子之規範。
units.en: The Founder was deeply filial: he never let his manner slip before the Empress Dowager and attended her at every meal, morning and night—a standard for the cultivated man.
units.literal: The Founder by nature was filial and reverent; in serving the Empress Dowager he never once showed the slightest lapse of countenance, morning and evening attending her meals—a model for gentlemen and scholars.

units.zh: 帝嚴察用法，無纖毫假貸，太后言之，帝頗為省刑。
units.en: The Emperor enforced the law without mercy; when the Empress Dowager intervened, he often eased sentences.
units.literal: The Emperor was strict in investigation and application of law, granting not the slightest indulgence; when the Empress Dowager spoke of it, the Emperor considerably lightened punishments.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖父誠蚤卒，有三子俱幼。
units.en: (The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 records that the Liang founder’s father Cheng died early, with three sons still small.
units.literal: (《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s father Cheng died young, leaving three sons all still young.

units.zh: 母王氏，攜養寄於同縣人劉崇家。
units.en: Their mother Wang entrusted the boys to Liu Chong, a man of the same county.
units.literal: The mother, née Wang, took them to be raised and lodged with Liu Chong of the same county.

units.zh: 昆弟之中，惟溫狡猾無行，崇母撫養之，崇兄弟嘗加譴杖。
units.en: Of the brothers only Wen was sly and unruly; Liu Chong’s mother cared for him, while Chong’s brothers often thrashed him.
units.literal: Among the brothers, only Wen was cunning and without proper conduct; Chong’s mother raised him, and Chong’s brothers sometimes beat him with rods.

units.zh: 一日，偷崇家釜而竄，為崇追回，崇母遮護，以免撲責。
units.en: Once he stole a pot from the Chong household and ran; caught and dragged back, he was spared the rod only because Chong’s mother stood between him and punishment.
units.literal: One day he stole a cauldron from Chong’s house and fled; Chong caught him and brought him back, but Chong’s mother shielded him so he escaped a beating.

units.zh: 善逐走鹿，往往及而獲之。
units.en: He could run down deer on foot and usually brought them down.
units.literal: He was skilled at chasing running deer and often overtook and caught them.

units.zh: 又，崇母常見其有龍蛇之異。
units.en: Liu Chong’s mother also claimed to see dragon-and-serpent portents about him.
units.literal: Moreover, Chong’s mother often saw in him omens of dragons and serpents.

units.zh: 他日與仲兄存入黃巢軍作賊，伯兄昱與母王氏尚依劉家。
units.en: Later Wen and his second brother Cun went off with Huang Chao’s rebels; the eldest, Yu, and Mother Wang remained with the Lius.
units.literal: Another day he and his second brother Cun joined Huang Chao’s army as bandits; the eldest brother Yu and their mother Wang still relied on the Liu household.

units.zh: 溫既辭去，不知存亡。
units.en: After Wen departed, his fate was unknown.
units.literal: Once Wen had left, none knew whether he lived or died.

units.zh: 及溫領鎮於汴，盛飾輿馬，使人迎母於崇家。
units.en: When Wen became military governor at Bian, he sent a splendid escort to bring his mother from the Chong home.
units.literal: When Wen held command at Bian, he lavishly adorned carriage and horses and sent men to welcome his mother from Chong’s house.

units.zh: 王氏惶恐，辭避深藏，不之信，謂人曰：「朱三落拓無行，何處作賊送死，焉能自致富貴？
units.en: Wang was afraid, refused, and hid; she told others: "That good-for-nothing Zhu Third is off robbing somewhere—how could he possibly have become rich and powerful?
units.literal: Wang was terrified, declined, and hid deep away, not believing it, and said to people: "Zhu Third is shiftless and without conduct—where is he playing bandit and courting death, that he could enrich himself and rise to nobility?

units.zh: 汴帥非吾子也。」
units.en: The lord of Bian cannot be my boy."
units.literal: The Bian commander is not my son."

units.zh: 使者具陳離鄉去裏之由，歸國立功之事，王氏方泣而信。
units.en: The envoy explained how Wen had left home, served the dynasty, and won distinction; at last Wang wept and believed.
units.literal: The messenger fully set forth the reasons for leaving home and native place and the deeds of returning to the state and achieving merit; only then did Wang weep and believe.

units.zh: 是日，與崇母並迎歸汴。
units.en: The same day both mothers were brought to Bian.
units.literal: That day she and Chong’s mother were both welcomed back to Bian.

units.zh: 溫盛禮郊迎，人士改觀。
units.en: Wen met them with full suburban ceremony, and onlookers saw him in a new light.
units.literal: Wen received them with grand rites at the suburban greeting; gentlemen changed their view of him.

units.zh: 崇以舊恩，位至列卿，為商州刺史。
units.en: For past kindness to the family, Chong rose to a chief-ministerial post and served as prefect of Shang.
units.literal: Chong, because of old kindness, rose to rank among chief ministers and became prefect of Shangzhou.

units.zh: 王氏以溫貴，封晉國太夫人。
units.en: With Wen’s rise, Wang was created Grand Lady of Jin.
units.literal: Because Wen had become noble, Wang was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.

units.zh: 仲兄存，於賊中為矢石所中而卒。
units.en: The second brother Cun died in the rebel ranks, killed by missile weapons.
units.literal: The second brother Cun, in the bandit army, was struck by arrow and stone and died.

units.zh: 溫置酒於母，歡甚，語及家事，謂母曰：「朱五經辛苦業儒，不登一命，今有子為節度使，無忝前人矣！」
units.en: At a feast for his mother Wen grew merry and said: "Father Zhu Five Classics studied the classics in poverty and never won office—yet his son is now a military commissioner. We have not shamed our ancestors!"
units.literal: Wen set out wine for his mother, very merry, and speaking of family affairs said to her: "Zhu Five Classics toiled at Confucian learning yet never received a single appointment; now there is a son who is military commissioner—no disgrace to our forebears!"

units.zh: 母不懌，良久謂溫曰：「汝致身及此，信為英特，行義未必如先人。
units.en: His mother was unmoved and after a pause told Wen: "You have risen high—no doubt you are gifted—but your conduct is hardly like your father’s.
units.literal: His mother was displeased and after a long while said to Wen: "You have reached this station—truly you are extraordinary—but in conduct you surely do not match your forebears.

units.zh: 朱二與汝同入賊軍，身死蠻徼，孤男稚女，艱食無告。
units.en: Your brother Zhu Second went into the rebels with you and died on the frontier; his widow and children are destitute, with no one to help them.
units.literal: Zhu Second entered the bandit army with you and died on the barbarian frontier; orphaned boys and young girls eat bitterly with none to plead for them.

units.zh: 汝未有恤孤之心，英特即有，諸無取也。」
units.en: You show no care for his orphans. Talent alone is nothing to boast of."
units.literal: You have not the heart to succor orphans—if you are extraordinary, still do not take pride in it."

units.zh: 溫垂涕謝罪，即令召諸兄子皆至汴。
units.en: Wen wept and apologized, then had every nephew brought to Bian.
units.literal: Wen shed tears and apologized, and at once ordered all his brothers’ sons summoned to Bian.

units.zh: 友寧、友倫皆立軍功，位至方鎮。）〉
units.en: Youning and Youlun both won military honors and rose to govern provinces.)〉
units.literal: Youning and Youlun both established military merit and reached posts as regional commissioners.)〉

units.zh: 元貞皇后張氏，乾化中追諡。
units.en: Empress Yuanzhen (Zhang) was posthumously honored during Qianhua.
units.literal: Empress Yuanzhen, née Zhang, was given a posthumous title in the Qianhua era.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：太祖皇后張氏早崩，開平二年，追封賢妃，至乾化二年十一月二十三日，追冊曰元貞皇后。
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that Empress Zhang died young; in Kaiping 2 she was posthumously made Worthy Consort, and on 23 xi of month 11, Qianhua 2, was elevated to Empress Yuanzhen.
units.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s empress Zhang died early; in Kaiping year 2 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Worthy Consort; on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month of Qianhua year 2 she was posthumously invested as Empress Yuanzhen.

units.zh: 又，《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖魏國夫人張氏，碭山富室女，父蕤，曾為宋州刺史。
units.en: The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 adds that Lady Zhang of Wei came from a rich Dangshan family; her father Rui had served as Songzhou prefect.
units.literal: Moreover, 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s Lady of Wei, née Zhang, was daughter of a wealthy house in Dangshan; her father Rui had once been prefect of Song.

units.zh: 溫時聞張有姿色，私心傾慕，有麗華之歎。
units.en: Hearing of Zhang’s beauty, Wen secretly yearned for her and sighed like a man longing for Lady Lihua.
units.literal: When Wen heard that Zhang had beauty, he secretly admired her and sighed with the lament of Lady Lihua.

units.zh: 及溫在同州，得張於兵間，因以婦禮納之。
units.en: At Tongzhou Wen took Zhang from among the captives and married her properly.
units.literal: When Wen was at Tongzhou he obtained Zhang amid the troops and took her in with the rites of a wife.

units.zh: 溫以其宿款，深加禮異。
units.en: Wen had loved her long before; he honored her with exceptional ceremony.
units.literal: Because of his long-standing affection, Wen treated her with deep courtesy and distinction.

units.zh: 張賢明有禮，溫雖虎狼其心，亦所景伏。
units.en: Zhang was intelligent and decorous; even Wen’s brutal nature bowed before her.
units.literal: Zhang was wise, clear, and observant of ritual; though Wen had the heart of a wolf or tiger, toward her he also bowed in awe.

units.zh: 每軍謀國計，必先延訪。
units.en: On every matter of war or statecraft he consulted her first.
units.literal: Whenever there was military planning or state policy, he first extended invitation to consult her.

units.zh: 或已出師，中途有所不可，張氏一介請旋，如期而至，其信重如此。
units.en: If a campaign had to be recalled mid-march, a single word from Zhang brought the army back on time—such was her authority.
units.literal: Even after the army had marched out, if midway something could not proceed, Zhang with a single message would request return—and arrived on the appointed day; such was the trust placed in her.

units.zh: 初收兗、鄆，得朱瑾妻，溫告之曰：「彼既無依，寓於輜車。」
units.en: After the capture of Yan and Yun they took Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her travel in the supply train."
units.literal: When Yan and Yun were first taken, they obtained Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her lodge in the baggage train."

units.zh: 張氏遣人召之，瑾妻再拜，張氏答拜泣下，謂之曰：「兗、鄆與司空同姓之國，昆仲之間，以小故尋戈，致吾姒如此。
units.en: Zhang sent for her; Jin’s wife bowed low, Zhang bowed back in tears and said: "Yan and Yun share our house’s surname—brothers quarreled over a trifle, and you, my sister-in-law, suffer for it.
units.literal: Zhang sent someone to summon her; Jin’s wife bowed twice, Zhang returned the bow weeping, and said to her: "Yan and Yun are states of the same surname as the Minister of Works; between brothers a small quarrel drew swords, and my sister-in-law has come to this.

units.zh: 設不幸汴州失守，妾亦似吾姒之今日也。」
units.en: Should Bian fall, I would share your fate."
units.literal: If by misfortune Bianzhou should fall, I too would be as my sister-in-law is today."

units.zh: 又泣下，乃度為尼，張恒給其費。
units.en: Weeping again, she had Jin’s wife take the veil and paid her upkeep.
units.literal: Again she wept, then had her tonsured as a nun; Zhang constantly supplied her expenses.

units.zh: 張既卒，繼寵者非人，及僭號後，大縱朋淫，骨肉聚麀，帷薄荒穢，以致友珪之禍，起於婦人。
units.en: After Zhang’s death Wen’s favorites were unworthy; once emperor he plunged into orgies and incest until Yougui’s revolt—born of a woman’s grievance.
units.literal: After Zhang died, those who succeeded her in favor were not worthy; after he assumed the imperial title he greatly indulged debauchery with companions, kin coupled like beasts, curtains and screens foul—so that Yougui’s disaster arose from a woman.

units.zh: 始能以柔婉之德，製豺虎之心，如張氏者，不亦賢乎！
units.en: At first, with soft grace she tamed a tiger’s heart—was Zhang not truly virtuous?
units.literal: To begin with, by gentle and yielding virtue to restrain the heart of wolf and tiger—as with Zhang—is she not worthy?

units.zh: 又，案《五代會要》所載，內職有梁太祖昭儀陳氏、昭容李氏，《歐陽史》並見《家人傳》。）〉
units.en: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 also lists the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li, both noted in Ouyang Xiu’s 《New History》 Family section.)〉
units.literal: Moreover, examining what the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records, among inner offices were the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li; both appear in 《Ouyang’s History》 in the Family Biographies.)〉

units.zh: 末帝德妃張氏。
units.en: Virtue Consort Zhang, consort of the Last Emperor.
units.literal: The Last Emperor’s Virtue Consort, née Zhang.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：少帝妃張氏，乾化五年九月二十四日，冊為德妃，其夕薨。
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that the Young Emperor’s consort Zhang was created Virtue Consort on 24 ix, Qianhua 5, and died the same night.
units.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Young Emperor’s consort Zhang, on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month of Qianhua year 5, was invested as Virtue Consort; that very evening she died.

units.zh: 案《歐陽史次妃郭氏傳》云：晉天福三年，詔太社先藏罪人首級，許親屬收葬，乃出末帝首，遣右衛將軍安崇阮與妃同葬。
units.en: Ouyang’s 《History》 biography of Consort Guo notes that in Tianfu 3 Jin permitted families to claim criminals’ heads from the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released and General An Chongruan buried it with his consort.
units.literal: Examining 《Ouyang’s History》, in the biography of the second consort Guo it says: In Jin Tianfu year 3 an edict allowed kin to bury heads of criminals long stored at the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was produced, and Right Palace Guard general An Chongruan was sent to bury it together with the consort.

units.zh: 妃卒洛陽。
units.en: She died at Luoyang.
units.literal: The consort died at Luoyang.

units.zh: 又案：《五代史》無外戚傳。
units.en: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 contains no treatise on imperial in-laws.
units.literal: Moreover, examining: 《History of the Five Dynasties》 has no biography of maternal kin.

units.zh: 《五代會要》云：梁太祖長女安陽公主，降羅廷規，開平二年八月追封。
units.en: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 lists the Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess Anyang, married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping 2, month 8.
units.literal: 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess of Anyang, was married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping year 2, eighth month.

units.zh: 長樂公主，降趙岩，開平元年五月十一日封。
units.en: Princess Changle wed Zhao Yan and was enfeoffed on 11 v, Kaiping 1.
units.literal: Princess of Changle was married to Zhao Yan and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.

units.zh: 普寧公主，降昭祚王氏，開平元年五月十一日封。
units.en: Princess Puning wed Wang Zhaozuo on the same date, 11 v, Kaiping 1.
units.literal: Princess of Puning was married to Wang Zhaozuo and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.

units.zh: 金華公主，開平二年十月封。
units.en: Princess Jinhua was enfeoffed in month 10, Kaiping 2.
units.literal: Princess of Jinhua was enfeoffed in the tenth month of Kaiping year 2.

units.zh: 真寧公主，乾化三年十月五日封。
units.en: Princess Zhenning was enfeoffed on 5 x, Qianhua 3.
units.literal: Princess of Zhenning was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the tenth month of Qianhua year 3.

units.zh: 少帝長女壽春公主，乾化三年四月五日封。
units.en: The Young Emperor’s eldest, Princess Shouchun, was enfeoffed on 5 iv, Qianhua 3.
units.literal: The Young Emperor’s eldest daughter, Princess of Shouchun, was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the fourth month of Qianhua year 3.

units.zh: 第二女壽昌公主，貞明元年九月二十三日封。
units.en: His second daughter, Princess Shouchang, was enfeoffed on 23 ix, Zhenming 1.
units.literal: His second daughter, Princess of Shouchang, was enfeoffed on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of Zhenming year 1.

units.zh: 今考《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣列傳》云：羅廷規尚安陽公主，又尚金華公主。
units.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 collation cites the 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married both Princess Anyang and Princess Jinhua.
units.literal: Now examining 《Comprehensive Mirror: Collation of Variants》, which cites 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married Princess of Anyang and also married Princess of Jinhua.

units.zh: 《薛史羅紹威傳》亦載開平四年，詔金華公主出家為尼。
units.en: The 《Old History》 biography of Luo Shaowei likewise records an edict in Kaiping 4 ordering Princess Jinhua to take the veil.
units.literal: 《Xue History》, biography of Luo Shaowei, also records that in Kaiping year 4 an edict had Princess of Jinhua leave the world and become a nun.

units.zh: 是金華公主實歸羅氏，而《五代會要》不載亦闕文也。）〉
units.en: So Jinhua truly married into the Luo house, though the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 omits it—another gap in the record.)〉
units.literal: Thus Princess of Jinhua in fact went to the Luo clan, while the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 does not record it—again a lacuna in the text.)〉

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：梁太祖自同州降唐，即依重榮，以母王氏，故事重榮為舅。）〉
units.en: (Ouyang Xiu notes the Founder called Chongrong uncle through Lady Wang.)〉
units.literal: (Ouyang Xiu's 《Historical Records》 says: Liang Founder from Tongzhou submitted to Tang and relied on Chongrong; because his mother was Lady Wang, by custom Chongrong was maternal uncle.)〉

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 次均王友貞，為東都馬步都指揮使。
units.en: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, commander of horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, Eastern Capital Horse and Foot Commander.

units.zh: 遣供奉官丁昭溥馳詣東都，命均王友貞殺友文。
units.en: He sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu in haste to the Eastern Capital to order Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.
units.literal: He dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital ordering Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.

units.zh: 梁祖在位止及六年，均帝朝詔史臣修梁祖實錄，岐下系鞋之事，恥而不書。
units.en: Taizu reigned only six years; under Emperor Jun historians were ordered to compile his veritable record—yet the shoe-tying at Qi was too shameful to write.
units.literal: Liang Taizu reigned only six years; in Emperor Jun’s reign an edict ordered historians to compile Taizu’s veritable record—the affair of tying shoes below Qi was shameful and not written.

units.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

units.zh: 乙酉，立皇兄全昱為廣王，皇子友文為博王，友珪為郢王，友璋為福王，友雍為賀王，友徽為建王。
units.en: On yiyou the Emperor enfeoffed his brother Quanyu as Prince of Guang and his sons Youwen, Yougui, Youzhang, Youyong, and Youhui as Princes of Bo, E, Fu, He, and Jian.
units.literal: On yiyou the Emperor's elder brother Quanyu was established as Prince of Guang, the imperial son Youwen as Prince of Bo, Yougui as Prince of E, Youzhang as Prince of Fu, Youyong as Prince of He, and Youhui as Prince of Jian.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 賴元貞皇后聞而召之，令束身歸汴，力為營救，太祖乃舍之，令權知許州。
units.en: Empress Yuanzhen intervened, had him return to Bian in custody, and secured his pardon; the Founder then put him in temporary charge of Xu.
units.literal: Relying on Empress Yuanzhen hearing and summoning him, ordered him to bind himself and return to Bian, vigorously pleading rescue; the Founder then released him, ordered temporary charge of Xu prefecture.

units.zh: 是時，元貞皇后賢而有寵，帝素憚之，由是不果攜歸大梁，因留亳州，以別宅貯之。
units.en: The Founder feared his capable consort Yuanzhen and never brought the woman to the capital, keeping her in a separate house at Bozhou.
units.literal: At the time Empress Yuanzhen was worthy and held favor; the Emperor always feared her, and therefore did not succeed in bringing [the mother] back to Great Liang, but left her at Bozhou, storing her in a separate residence.

units.zh: 景福元年，總大軍伐徐。
units.en: In Jingfu 1 he led the main force against Xu.
units.literal: Jingfu year 1, commanded the great army to attack Xu.

units.zh: 唐光啟中，帝徇地亳州，召而侍寢。
units.en: During Tang Guangqi, while campaigning in Bozhou, the Founder took her to his bed.
units.literal: In the Guangqi era of Tang, the Emperor toured Bozhou territory, summoned her to attend his bed.

units.zh: 考诚谥曰文穆，庙号烈祖，妣王氏谥曰文惠。
units.en: his father Cheng the name Wen Mu and temple name Ancestor Lie, and his mother of the Wang clan the name Wen Hui.
units.literal: his father Cheng the title Wen Mu and temple name Liezu, and his mother the Wang clan the title Wen Hui.

units.zh: 秋七月己亥，追尊祖考为皇帝，妣为皇后；
units.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jihai, he posthumously honored his forebears as emperors and their consorts as empresses;
units.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jihai day, his ancestors and father were posthumously honored as emperors and his mother as empress;

units.zh: 時租庸使趙岩勸帝郊天，且言：「帝王受命，須行此禮，願陛下力行之。」
units.en: Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged Heaven-sacrifice, saying: "Emperors who receive the Mandate must perform this rite—Your Majesty should see it through."
units.literal: At the time Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged the Emperor to sacrifice to Heaven, saying: "When emperors receive the Mandate they must perform this rite; Your Majesty should exert yourself to carry it out."

units.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

units.zh: 己巳，帝幸洛陽，為來年有事於南郊也。
units.en: On jisi the Emperor went to Luoyang to prepare for a Southern Suburban rite the following year.
units.literal: On jisi the Emperor visited Luoyang, because next year there would be affairs at the Southern Suburban Altar.

units.zh: 時朱瑾領兗、鄆之眾，為徐戎外援，陣於彭門南石佛山下。
units.en: Zhu Jin of Yan and Yun brought allied troops to aid Xu and drew up south of Pengmen at Stone Buddha Mountain.
units.literal: At the time Zhu Jin led Yan and Yun hosts as outer support for Xu bandits, arrayed below Stone Buddha Mountain south of Peng Gate.

units.zh: 友裕縱兵擊之，斬獲甚眾，瑾領殘黨宵遁。
units.en: You Yu attacked, inflicted heavy losses, and Jin fled by night with the survivors.
units.literal: You Yu loosed troops to strike them, beheading and capturing very many; Jin led the remnant party to flee by night.

units.zh: 式請鎔子昭祚及大將梁公儒、李宏規子各一人往質於汴。
units.en: Shi requested that Rong's son Zhaozhuo and one son each of the great generals Liang Gongru and Li Honggui be sent as hostages to Bian.
units.literal: Shi requested that Rong's son Zhaozhuo and one son each of the great generals Liang Gongru and Li Honggui go as hostages to Bian.

units.zh: 鎔長子昭祚，亂之翌日，張文禮索之，斬於軍門。
units.en: Rong's eldest son Zhaozhuo was demanded by Zhang Wenli the day after the uprising and beheaded at the army gate.
units.literal: Rong's eldest son Zhaozhuo, on the day after the uprising, was demanded by Zhang Wenli and beheaded at the army gate.

units.zh: 梁祖以女妻昭祚。
units.en: The Founding Emperor of Liang married his daughter to Zhaozhuo.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor of Liang gave his daughter in marriage to Zhaozhuo.

units.zh: 是日，令其子昭祚與張文禮以兵圍李宏規及行軍司馬李藹宅，並族誅之，詿誤者凡數十家。
units.en: That day he ordered his son Zhaozhuo and Zhang Wenli to surround the residences of Li Honggui and the campaign secretary Li Ai with troops, executed their entire clans, and implicated several dozen households by error.
units.literal: That day he ordered his son Zhaozhuo and Zhang Wenli to surround with troops the residences of Li Honggui and the campaign secretary Li Ai, executed their entire clans, and those implicated by error numbered several tens of households.

units.zh: 節度使羅紹威以帝回軍，慮有不測之患，由是供億甚至，因密以天人之望切陳之。
units.en: Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei, fearing trouble when the Emperor marched home with his army, supplied provisions lavishly and privately urged that Heaven and men alike expected the transfer of the mandate.
units.literal: Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei, because the Emperor was returning with his army, feared unforeseen trouble; he therefore supplied provisions on an extraordinary scale and privately urged him in the strongest terms that Heaven and men alike expected his next step.

units.zh: 帝雖拒而不納，然心德之。
units.en: The Emperor refused but was inwardly grateful.
units.literal: The Emperor declined but was inwardly grateful.

units.zh: 全忠女妻威子廷規，先是卒。
units.en: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui and had died earlier.
units.literal: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had died earlier.

units.zh: 時右衛上將軍婁繼英請之，會繼英得罪，乃詔左衛上將軍安崇阮收葬焉。
units.en: Lou Jiying requested the head; when he fell from favor, An Chongruan of the Left Guard was ordered to bury it.
units.literal: At the time Right Guard senior general Lou Jiying requested it; when Jiying fell into guilt, an edict ordered Left Guard senior general An Chongruan to collect and bury it.

units.zh: 晉天福二年五月，詔太社先藏唐朝罪人首級，許親屬及舊僚收葬。
units.en: In Tianfu 2 of Later Jin, kin and former officials might reclaim Tang heads stored at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: In the fifth month of Tianfu 2 of Jin, an edict said that heads of Tang criminals formerly stored at the Grand Altar might be reclaimed by kin and old subordinates.

units.zh: 密王友倫，幼聰悟，喜筆劄，曉聲律。
units.en: You Lun, Prince of Mi, was bright as a child, loved literature, and had an ear for music.
units.literal: Prince of Mi You Lun, in youth clever and perceptive, delighted in letters, understood musical tones.

units.zh: 太祖征兗、鄆，友倫勒所部兵收聚糧穀，以濟軍須。
units.en: During campaigns in Yan and Yun he gathered grain for the army.
units.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Yan and Yun, You Lun led his troops to gather grain to supply the army.

units.zh: 幽、滄軍至內黃，友倫前鋒夜渡河擊賊，奪馬千匹，擒斬甚眾。
units.en: When Youzhou and Cangzhou forces reached Neihuang, his vanguard crossed the river at night, took a thousand horses, and killed or captured many.
units.literal: You and Cang troops reached Neihuang; You Lun's vanguard crossed the river by night to strike bandits, seizing a thousand horses, capturing and beheading many.

units.zh: 因引兵往八議關，卒逢晉軍萬餘騎，友倫乃分布兵士，多設疑軍。
units.en: Marching toward Bayi Pass he met more than ten thousand Jin horsemen and spread his men in feigned formations.
units.literal: Thereupon he led troops toward Bayi Pass, suddenly encountering more than ten thousand Jin cavalry; You Lun then distributed soldiers, setting many decoy units.

units.zh: 太祖遣友倫總步騎數萬，越險救應，遂大破晉軍。
units.en: The Founder sent You Lun with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry over difficult ground to relieve him and routed the Jin army.
units.literal: The Founder dispatched You Lun to command several tens of thousands of foot and horse, crossing rugged terrain to rescue and respond, and greatly defeated Jin troops.

units.zh: 友倫率徒兵三萬徑往礬山，晉人望塵奔逸。
units.en: You Lun marched thirty thousand foot soldiers to Fanshan and the Jin army fled at his approach.
units.literal: You Lun led thirty thousand foot soldiers straight to Fanshan; Jin men fled at sight of dust.

units.zh: 友倫與氏叔琮等躡其轍，追至太原，摩壘挑戰，獲牛馬萬餘。
units.en: With Shi Shuzong he pursued to Taiyuan, challenged the walls, and seized more than ten thousand cattle and horses.
units.literal: You Lun with Shi Shuzong and others followed their tracks, pursuing to Taiyuan, pressing the ramparts and challenging battle, obtaining more than ten thousand cattle and horses.

units.zh: 三年，昭宗歸長安，製授友倫寧遠軍節度使、檢校司徒，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。
units.en: In the third year, after Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, You Lun became Ningyuan military commissioner and acting Minister of Works with the honorific Welcoming-the-Carriage Resolute Warrior.
units.literal: Year 3, Zhaozong returned to Chang'an; by decree You Lun was made military commissioner of the Ningyuan Army, acting Minister of Works, granted the title Meritous Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.

units.zh: 及太祖東歸，留友倫宿衛京師。
units.en: When the Founder went east he left You Lun to guard the capital.
units.literal: When the Founder returned east, he left You Lun to garrison and guard the capital.

units.zh: 皇侄故邕州節度使友寧、故容州節度使友倫，頃因締構，俱習韜鈐，並以戰功，歿於王事，永言帶礪，合議封崇。」
units.en: Imperial nephews You Ning, late commissioner of Yong, and You Lun, late commissioner of Rong, were trained in war from the founding days and died in service; they deserve posthumous honors befitting founders of the house."
units.literal: Imperial nephew, late Yongzhou military commissioner You Ning, late Rongzhou military commissioner You Lun—recently because of founding the structure, both studied military manuals, and both through battle merit died in royal service; forever speaking of belt and flint, together we should discuss enfeoffment and elevation."

units.zh: 於是存追封朗王，友寧追封安王，友倫追封密王。
units.en: Cun was posthumously created Prince of Lang, You Ning Prince of An, and You Lun Prince of Mi.
units.literal: Thereupon Cun was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lang, You Ning posthumously Prince of An, You Lun posthumously Prince of Mi.

units.zh: 年十九，為宣武軍校。
units.en: He entered the Xuanwu Army as an officer at nineteen.
units.literal: At nineteen he became an officer of the Xuanwu Army.

units.zh: 景福初，充元從騎軍都將，尋表為右武衛將軍，漸委戎事。
units.en: Early in Jingfu he commanded the emperor's mounted guard, was soon made Right Martial Guard general, and gradually took on field command.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, he served as commander of the personal cavalry guard; soon memorialized as Right Martial Guard general, gradually entrusted with military affairs.

units.zh: 天復元年，岐、隴用兵，晉人乘虛侵於北鄙。
units.en: In Tianfu 1, while war raged at Qi and Long, Jin raiders struck the northern border.
units.literal: In Tianfu year 1, troops were used at Qi and Long; Jin men took advantage of emptiness to invade the northern frontier.

units.zh: 歲餘，因會賓擊鞠，墜馬而卒。
units.en: More than a year later he fell from his horse during a polo match with guests and died.
units.literal: After more than a year, while meeting guests playing cuju, he fell from a horse and died.

units.zh: 昭宗輟視朝一日，詔贈太傅，歸葬於碭山縣。
units.en: Zhaozong mourned him with a day without court and posthumously made him Grand Tutor; he was buried in Dangshan.
units.literal: Zhaozong suspended court audience for one day, edict posthumously gave Grand Tutor, burial returned to Dangshan county.

units.zh: 及長，好騎射，有經度之智，太祖每奇之，曰：「吾家千里駒也。」
units.en: As a man he excelled at horsemanship and archery and showed sound judgment; the Founder often praised him: "He is the fleet steed of our clan."
units.literal: When grown, he loved riding and shooting, had the wisdom of governance; the Founder often marveled at him, saying: "A thousand-li colt of our house."

units.zh: 安王友寧，字安仁，少習詩禮，長喜兵法，有倜儻之風。
units.en: You Ning, Prince of An (courtesy name Anren), studied the classics as a boy and warfare as a man, with a dashing temper.
units.literal: Prince of An You Ning, style Anren, in youth studied Poetry and Rites, in maturity delighted in military methods, had a bold and unbounded air.

units.zh: 及擒秦宗權，太祖令友寧監送宗權西獻於長安，詔加檢校右散騎常侍、行右監門衛將軍。
units.en: After the capture of Qin Zongquan the Founder sent You Ning to escort him to Chang'an; the court promoted him to acting palace attendant and acting gate guard commander.
units.literal: When Qin Zongquan was captured, the Founder ordered You Ning to supervise escorting Zongquan west to present at Chang'an; edict added acting Right Palace Attendant and Acting Right Supervisor of the Palace Gate Guards.

units.zh: 太祖駐軍岐下，遣友寧領所部兵先歸梁苑，以備守禦。
units.en: While the Founder camped near Qi he sent You Ning ahead with his division to secure the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: The Founder encamped below Qi, dispatched You Ning to lead his troops first back to Liang Garden to prepare defense.

units.zh: 會有青人詣裴迪言其狀，迪以事告，友寧不俟命乃率兵萬餘人東討。
units.en: A Qing informer told Pei Di, who reported to You Ning; without waiting for orders You Ning marched east with ten thousand men.
units.literal: It happened a man of Qing came to Pei Di and reported the situation; Di told the affair, and You Ning without awaiting orders led more than ten thousand troops east to punish.

units.zh: 友寧引兵救之，青寇大敗，奪馬四千蹄，斬首數千級。
units.en: You Ning relieved the city and routed the Qing forces, taking four thousand horses and thousands of heads.
units.literal: You Ning led troops to rescue; Qing bandits were greatly defeated, seizing four thousand horse hooves, beheading several thousand.

units.zh: 及昭宗歸長安，朝廷議迎駕功，友寧授嶺南西道節度使，加特進、檢校司徒，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。
units.en: After Emperor Zhaozong's return to Chang'an the court rewarded those who had escorted him: You Ning became military commissioner of Lingnan West, Special Grandee, and acting Minister of Works, with the honorific Welcoming-the-Carriage Resolute Warrior.
units.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, the court discussed merit in welcoming the imperial carriage; You Ning was given military commissioner of Lingnan West Circuit, advanced to Special Grandee and acting Minister of Works, granted the title Meritous Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.

units.zh: 友寧知之，伏兵於兗南邀之，大破賊眾，竟無免者。
units.en: You Ning set an ambush south of Yan, destroyed the force, and left no survivor.
units.literal: You Ning knew it, ambushed troops south of Yan to intercept them, greatly defeating the bandit host; in the end none escaped.

units.zh: 自是兗壁危窘，友寧督諸軍進逼營兵。
units.en: With Yanzhou hard pressed, You Ning drove his columns against the rebel encampment.
units.literal: From then on the Yan ramparts were perilous and strained; You Ning supervised the armies pressing the rebel camp.

units.zh: 友寧乃下俘民眾十餘萬，各領負木石、牽牛驢，於城南為土山。
units.en: You Ning drove more than a hundred thousand captives—each hauling timber and stone behind oxen and donkeys—to heap an assault ramp south of the walls.
units.literal: You Ning then released more than a hundred thousand captive common people, each leading and bearing timber and stone, driving oxen and donkeys, building an earthen mound south of the city.

units.zh: 及進迫寇壘，與青人戰於石樓，王師小卻，友寧旁自峻阜馳騎以赴敵，所乘馬蹶而仆，遂沒於陣。
units.en: Pressing the rebel stronghold at Shilou, he charged from a ridge when the royal army slightly wavered; his horse fell and he died in the melee.
units.literal: When advancing to press the rebel fortress, fighting Qing troops at Shilou, Wang's army slightly retreated; You Ning from a steep height galloped to meet the enemy, his mount stumbled and fell, and he perished in the formation.

units.zh: 友寧將戰之前日，有大白蛇蟠於帳中，友寧心惡之，既而果遇禍焉。
units.en: On the eve of battle a great white snake coiled in his tent—an omen he loathed—and the next day he was killed.
units.literal: The day before You Ning was to fight, a great white serpent coiled in his tent; You Ning's heart hated it, and afterward he indeed met calamity.

units.zh: 太祖鎮汴，累署軍職，每因出師，多命統驍果以從。
units.en: Under the Founder's rule at Bian he rose through army commands and usually led elite troops on campaign.
units.literal: When the Founder governed Bian, repeatedly appointed to army posts; whenever campaigns arose he was often ordered to lead fierce warriors in attendance.

units.zh: 俄而城陷，盡屠其邑人，清河為之不流。
units.en: The city soon fell and every inhabitant was massacred until the Qing River ran thick with blood.
units.literal: Shortly the city fell; the entire populace of the district was slaughtered, and the Qing River ceased to flow.

units.zh: 時安陽公主初卒於魏，太祖乃遺嗣勳率長直官千人，實兵仗於橐中，肩舁以入於魏，聲言來致祭會葬，牙軍不之覺。
units.en: Princess Anyang had just died at Wei; the Founder sent Sixun with a thousand hand-picked men, weapons hidden in coffers carried on poles into the city under cover of funeral rites, and the guard army never suspected.
units.literal: At the time Princess Anyang had just died in Wei; the Founder then sent Sixun leading a thousand long-guard officers, with weapons packed in chests and borne on shoulders into Wei, declaring they came to offer sacrifice at the funeral—the guard army did not notice.

units.zh: 天祐三年正月十六日夜，嗣勳與紹威親軍同攻牙軍，至曙，盡殪之。
units.en: On the night of the sixteenth of the first month of Tianyou 3, Sixun and Shaowei's own troops struck the guard corps and wiped them out by dawn.
units.literal: Tianyou 3 first month, night of the sixteenth, Sixun with Shaowei's personal troops together attacked the guard army; by dawn they were all annihilated.

units.zh: 後主沈皇后 張貴妃
units.en: Last Emperor Empress Shen; Noble Consort Zhang
units.literal: Last Emperor Empress Shen; Noble Consort Zhang

units.zh: 後主貴妃張麗華
units.en: Last Emperor Noble Consort Zhang Lihua
units.literal: Last Emperor Noble Consort Zhang Lihua

units.zh: 後主張貴妃名麗華，兵家女也。
units.en: Noble Consort Zhang of the Last Emperor, named Lihua, was the daughter of a military household.
units.literal: Noble Consort Zhang of the Last Emperor, named Lihua, was the daughter of a military household.

units.zh: 後主自居臨春閣，張貴妃居結綺閣，龔、孔二貴嬪居望仙閣，嵭復道交相往來。
units.en: The Last Emperor lived in the Linchun Pavilion, Precious Consort Zhang in the Jieqi Pavilion, and Honored Consorts Gong and Kong in the Wangxian Pavilion, with skyways connecting them for constant visits.
units.literal: The Last Emperor himself dwelt in the Linchun Pavilion; Precious Consort Zhang in the Jieqi Pavilion; the two honored consorts Gong and Kong in the Wangxian Pavilion; elevated passageways linked them so they could come and go to one another.

units.zh: 後主即位，拜為貴妃。
units.en: When the Last Emperor came to the throne, she was appointed noble consort.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, she was appointed noble consort.

units.zh: 高祖章皇后 世祖沈皇后 廢帝王皇后 高宗柳皇后
units.en: Founder Empress Zhang; Emperor Wen Empress Shen; Deposed Emperor Empress Wang; Emperor Xuan Empress Liu
units.literal: Founder Empress Zhang; Emperor Wen Empress Shen; Deposed Emperor Empress Wang; Emperor Xuan Empress Liu

units.zh: 是時龔貴嬪為良娣，貴妃年十歲，為之給使，後主見而說焉，因得幸，遂有娠，生太子深。
units.en: At the time Honored Consort Gong was liangdi, and the noble consort, then ten, served her. The Last Emperor saw and liked her, so she gained his favor, became pregnant, and gave birth to Crown Prince Shen.
units.literal: At this time Honored Consort Gong was liangdi, and the noble consort, aged ten, served her; the Last Emperor saw her and liked her, so she gained favor, became pregnant, and gave birth to Crown Prince Shen.

units.zh: 家貧，父兄以織席為事。
units.en: Her family was poor, and her father and elder brothers made a living weaving mats.
units.literal: Her family was poor, and her father and elder brothers made a living weaving mats.

units.zh: 及隋軍陷臺城，妃與後主俱入于井，隋軍出之，晉王廣命斬貴妃，牓於青溪中橋。
units.en: When the Sui army took Taicheng, the consort and the Last Emperor hid together in a well. Sui soldiers brought them out, and Guang, Prince of Jin, ordered the noble consort beheaded and displayed at the middle bridge over Qingxi.
units.literal: When the Sui army took Taicheng, the consort and the Last Emperor both entered a well; Sui soldiers brought them out, and Guang, Prince of Jin, ordered the noble consort beheaded and displayed at the middle bridge over Qingxi.

units.zh: 而張貴妃髮長七尺，鬒黑如漆，其光可鑒。
units.en: Precious Consort Zhang's hair was seven feet long, black as lacquer and bright enough to mirror one's face.
units.literal: Yet Precious Consort Zhang's hair was seven feet long, black as lacquer, its luster mirror-bright.

units.zh: 李、蔡所不能記者，貴妃嵭為條疏，無所遺脫。
units.en: What Li and Cai forgot, the Precious Consort would lay out in clear lists without omission.
units.literal: What Li and Cai could not remember, the Precious Consort would set out in ordered lists, omitting nothing.

units.zh: 後主遇后既薄，而張貴妃寵傾後宮，後宮之政嵭歸之，后澹然未嘗有所忌怨。
units.en: The Last Emperor treated the empress coldly, while Noble Consort Zhang dominated the harem in favor and all inner-palace affairs passed to her. The empress remained calm and never showed jealousy or resentment.
units.literal: The Last Emperor treated the empress coldly, while Noble Consort Zhang's favor dominated the rear palace and all inner-palace government went to her; the empress remained calm and never showed jealousy or resentment.

units.zh: 史臣侍中鄭國公魏徵考覽記書，參詳故老，云後主初即位，以始興王叔陵之亂，被傷臥于承香閣下，時諸姬嵭不得進，唯張貴妃侍焉。
units.en: The historiographer, palace attendant and Duke of Zheng, Wei Zheng, examined the records and consulted elders and wrote: When the Last Emperor first succeeded, he was wounded in the disorder of Prince of Shixing Shuling and lay ill below the Hall of Accepting Fragrance; none of the palace women could enter—only Noble Consort Zhang attended him.
units.literal: The historiographer, Palace Attendant and Duke of Zheng, Wei Zheng, examined records and consulted elders, saying: When the Last Emperor first took the throne, because of the disorder of Prince of Shixing Shuling, he was wounded and lay ill below the Hall of Accepting Fragrance; at that time none of the ladies could enter—only Noble Consort Zhang attended him.

units.zh: 後主每引賓客對貴妃等遊宴，則使諸貴人及女學士與狎客共賦新詩，互相贈答，採其尤豔麗者以為曲詞，被以新聲，選宮女有容色者以千百數，令習而哥之，[8]分部迭進，持以相樂。
units.en: Whenever the Last Emperor feasted with guests and the Precious Consort, he had the ladies and female academicians join familiar companions in new verse, trading lines; the finest were set as lyrics to new music, and hundreds or thousands of comely palace women were drilled to sing them—[8] sections took turns performing for the revel.
units.literal: Whenever the Last Emperor led guests to feast with the Precious Consort and the others, he would have the various ladies and female academicians join intimates in composing new poems and exchanging verses; the most gorgeous were chosen for song lyrics, set to new tunes; palace women of pleasing looks were selected by the hundreds and thousands and made to study and sing them; [8] by sections they advanced in rotation, holding revel together.

units.zh: 其曲有玉樹後庭花、臨春樂等，大指所歸，皆美張貴妃、孔貴嬪之容色也。
units.en: Tunes such as "Jade Tree, Rear-Court Blossom" and "Linchun Joy" chiefly praised the beauty of Precious Consort Zhang and Honored Consort Kong.
units.literal: Among the tunes were "Jade Tree, Rear-Court Blossom" and "Linchun Joy"; their drift in general praised the looks of Precious Consort Zhang and Honored Consort Kong.

units.zh: 是時，後主怠於政事，百司啟奏，嵭因宦者蔡脫兒、李善度進請，[9]後主置張貴妃於膝上共決之。
units.en: The Last Emperor had grown slack in rule; memorials from every office came only through eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu—[9] and he set Precious Consort Zhang on his knee to decide them with him.
units.literal: At that time the Last Emperor neglected government; when the hundred offices submitted memorials they all reached him through the eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu; [9] he seated Precious Consort Zhang on his lap to decide them together.

units.zh: 而後宮之家，不遵法度，有挂於理者，但求哀於貴妃，貴妃則令李、蔡先啟其事，而後從容為言之。
units.en: Inner-palace families who broke the law would beg the Precious Consort's mercy; she had Li and Cai raise the case first, then spoke for them at leisure.
units.literal: When households of the inner palace broke the law and were at fault in principle, they need only plead with the Precious Consort; she would have Li and Cai first report the matter, then calmly speak for them.

units.zh: 於是張、孔之勢，薰灼四方，大臣執政，亦從風而靡。
units.en: Zhang and Kong's influence blazed everywhere, and ministers in power bent with the wind.
units.literal: Thus the power of Zhang and Kong scorched all directions; ministers in charge also bowed before the wind.

units.zh: 尋間道告於梁曰：「王氏喪於亂軍，普寧公主無恙。」
units.en: she soon sent word by a secret path to the Liang: "The Wang house has fallen to mutineers, but Princess Puning is safe."
units.literal: soon by a hidden route she reported to the Liang: "The Wang house has perished among the mutinous troops; Princess Puning is unharmed."

units.zh: 是夜作亂，殺王鎔父子，舉族灰滅，惟留王昭祚妻朱氏通梁人；
units.en: That night they rose in mutiny, killed Wang Rong and his son, and annihilated the clan—only Zhaozuo's wife Lady Zhu, who had connections with the Liang, was spared;
units.literal: That night they mutinied, killed Wang Rong father and son, and wiped out the whole clan to ashes; only Wang Zhaozuo's wife the Lady Zhu, who had ties to Liang men, was spared;
